extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and advanced undergraduates studying algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea')
extracted.subtask_description: Defining and checking morphisms between schemes via ringed/locally ringed spaces and affine-local descriptions; understanding associated constructions (pushforward/pullback of O-modules, maps from graded rings, rational maps, functor of points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a morphism of ringed spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of ringed spaces π : X → Y is a continuous map of topological spaces π together with a map OY → π_* OX (equivalently π^{-1} OY → OX) which is thought of as a “pullback map”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be packaged using adjointness; composition and category structure follow. The text notes it's convenient to use either formulation (direct or via adjointness) and references a diagram (2.7.2.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open embedding (open immersion) of ringed spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: If U ⊂ Y is an open subset and U is identified (isomorphic) with an open subset V of Y, then the resulting map of ringed spaces (U, OY|U) → (Y, OY) (via the isomorphism) is called an open embedding (or open immersion) of ringed spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notation U ↪ Y (often written U ≃ V ↪ Y) is used; open embeddings are later shown to be monomorphisms (Exercise 7.2.B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing morphisms of ringed spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an open cover X = ⋃i Ui and morphisms πi : Ui → Y that agree on overlaps (πi|Ui∩Uj = πj|Ui∩Uj), there is a unique morphism π : X → Y restricting to the πi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 7.2.A. This is the analogue of gluing maps of topological spaces and is essential for constructing global morphisms from local data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open embeddings are monomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Open embeddings of ringed spaces are monomorphisms in the category of ringed spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as Exercise 7.2.B; implies uniqueness properties when embedding opens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushforward of O-modules (functoriality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a morphism of ringed spaces π : X → Y, sheaf pushforward induces a functor Mod OX → Mod OY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 7.2.C. This is the standard direct image functor for modules over structure sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback of O-modules (definition and properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given π : (X, OX) → (Y, OY), the pullback π^* of an OY-module G is constructed by first taking π^{-1}G (a π^{-1}OY-module) and then tensoring: π^*G = π^{-1}G ⊗_{π^{-1}OY} OX, yielding an OX-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 7.2.D: show π^* is covariant, functorial, composes appropriately (ρ^* π^* ≅ (π ◦ ρ)^*), and is left-adjoint to π_* (describe natural bijection Hom_X(π^* G, F) ≅ Hom_Y(G, π_* F)). Also define push-pull maps in commutative diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map on stalks for a morphism of ringed spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Given π : X → Y and p ∈ X with π(p)=q, there is an induced map on stalks (OY)_q → (OX)_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 7.2.E. This is the local description of the sheaf morphism and is used repeatedly to analyze behavior at points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine scheme morphism from a ring homomorphism (construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a ring map π^#: B → A, one defines a morphism of ringed spaces π : Spec A → Spec B by the underlying topological map and by defining the map on the distinguished basis via OSpec B(D(g)) → OSpec A(D(π^# g)) = A_{π^# g}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key Exercise 7.2.F: verify independence of choices and that this describes a morphism of sheaves on the distinguished base; this is the basic way ring maps induce scheme maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tentative affine-local definition of morphism of schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of schemes should 'locally look like' the maps of affine schemes coming from ring maps: for each choice of affine open Spec A ⊂ X and Spec B ⊂ Y with π(Spec A) ⊂ Spec B, the induced map should be of the form coming from a ring homomorphism B → A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 7.2.2 describes this tentative definition; the text prefers to use locally ringed spaces to formalize and then use affine covers in practice (see later exercises).

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphism of locally ringed spaces (local-ring condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of locally ringed spaces π : X → Y is a morphism of ringed spaces such that the induced map on stalks π^#: OY,q → OX,p sends the maximal ideal m_{Y,q} into the maximal ideal m_{X,p} (i.e., is a local homomorphism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 7.3.1. This condition encodes the intuition that values of functions pull back: zeros map to zeros, nonzeros to nonzeros, and ensures residue-field inclusion κ(q) → κ(p).

rubrics_metrics.name: Values of functions pull back under locally ringed-space morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is a morphism of locally ringed spaces with π(p)=q, then π induces an inclusion of residue fields κ(q) ↪ κ(p), and the locus where a function is zero (or nonzero) pulls back to the locus where the pulled-back function is zero (or nonzero).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 7.3.A and associated discussion: captures concretely that functions have values at points and those values behave functorially under pullback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: morphism of schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and Y are schemes, a morphism π : X → Y is a morphism of locally ringed spaces. The category of schemes Sch is defined using these morphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 7.3.3. After this, isomorphisms and automorphisms of schemes are the obvious notions from locally ringed-space maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms between affines determined by maps on global sections
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : Spec A → Spec B is a morphism of locally ringed spaces, then it is induced by the ring map π^#: B = Γ(Spec B, O) → Γ(Spec A, O) = A (i.e., morphisms of affines correspond to ring homomorphisms in the opposite direction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key Proposition 7.3.2 and Exercise 7.3.C: the map on global sections determines both the map on points and the map on structure sheaves (check on distinguished opens).

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking morphisms on affine covers (affine-local checking)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of schemes π : X → Y is a morphism of ringed spaces that looks locally like morphisms of affine schemes; it suffices to check on pairs (Spec A_i, Spec B_j) where the Spec A_i cover X and the Spec B_j cover Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 7.3.D: in practice one uses affine covers to define and verify morphisms and then forgets the locally ringed-space formalism for computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms to affine schemes correspond to ring homomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Morphisms X → Spec A are in natural bijection with ring morphisms A → Γ(X, OX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential Exercise 7.3.G: prove first for affine X then glue. Consequence: canonical morphism X → Spec Γ(X,O_X); it is an isomorphism iff X is affine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure morphism and category of S-schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: An S-scheme is a morphism X → S (the structure morphism); morphisms of S-schemes are commutative diagrams over S (i.e., maps X → Y compatible with structure maps to S).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 7.3.7: when S=Spec A this recovers A-schemes. This viewpoint organizes families and base change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final/initial objects and basic categorical facts in Sch
rubrics_metrics.description: Spec Z is the final object in the category of schemes (unique morphism X → Spec Z for any X); likewise, Spec A is final in the category of A-schemes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 7.3.J: standard categorical observations used frequently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coproducts (disjoint unions) in Sch
rubrics_metrics.description: The disjoint union X ⨿ Y (as in Exercise 4.3.E) is the coproduct of schemes X and Y in the category of schemes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 7.3.K: helpful when building schemes by gluing components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical morphisms from local and residue-field spectra
rubrics_metrics.description: For a point p of a scheme X there is a canonical morphism Spec O_{X,p} → X (choice-free); likewise a canonical morphism Spec κ(p) → X giving p the interpretation as a scheme-point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 7.3.L and 7.3.M: moreover, Mor(Spec A, X) (A local) corresponds bijectively to pairs (p ∈ X, local homomorphisms O_{X,p} → A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functor of points (scheme-valued points)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a scheme Z, Z-valued points of X are X(Z) = Hom(Z, X). For a ring A, A-valued points X(A) are X(Spec A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 7.3.10: this viewpoint interprets schemes as functors and is essential for Yoneda-style arguments; caution about terminology (Z-valued 'points' need not be literal points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms determined by induced maps on all Z-valued points
rubrics_metrics.description: While morphisms of schemes are not determined by their underlying map on topological points, they are determined by the induced maps X(Z) → Y(Z) on Z-valued points as Z varies over all schemes (pick Z=X to recover the map).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 7.3.N: essentially an instance of Yoneda's Lemma in this context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maps to projective schemes from graded-ring maps / homogeneous functions
rubrics_metrics.description: A map φ: S → R of graded rings (graded-map with degree-multiplying d) induces a morphism Proj R \ V(φ(S_+)) → Proj S; if V(φ(S_+)) is empty, one gets a global map Proj R → Proj S. Equivalently, n+1 homogeneous functions on X with no common zeros give a morphism X → P^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential Exercise 7.4.A and 7.3.O: to construct maps to projective space one often either uses graded ring maps or n+1 homogeneous sections (or later, sections of a line bundle). Various caveats: not every graded-ring map yields a global map, different graded maps can give the same map of schemes, and regrading (Veronese) can often reduce to degree-1 generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veronese subring / regrading trick
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a finitely generated graded ring S, the d-th Veronese subring S^{(d)} = ⊕_{j≥0} S_{jd} defines a regrading that can be used so that after passing to some Veronese subring one may assume generation in degree 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 7.4.D–7.4.G: this allows embedding Proj into projective space by reducing to degree-1-generated rings (useful for avoiding finite-degree pathologies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of rational map between reduced schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: A rational map π : X ⇢ Y (for X reduced) is an equivalence class of morphisms α: U → Y where U ⊂ X is a dense open; two representatives (α: U, β: V) are equivalent if they agree on some dense open subset of U ∩ V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 7.5.1: think of rational maps as morphisms defined 'almost everywhere'; later results (for separated targets, irreducible sources) give uniqueness and maximal domains of definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dominant rational maps and criterion for irreducible schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: A rational map π : X ⇢ Y is dominant if its image is dense in Y (equivalently for any representative α: U → Y the image is dense). For irreducible schemes, π is dominant iff it sends the generic point of X to the generic point of Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 7.5.B: dominance is a topological/dominance property often rephrased in terms of generic points when schemes are irreducible.
